cells: BIVARIATE DECISIONS  |  What does the student's actual scatter show?
Display ONLY after paired numerical observations have been plotted and the student has described the pattern. Earlier prediction, chosen PMCC and course choice are context—not evidence of a result.
Short default: 'What do you see?' → choose one of four observed patterns or Not sure → 'What mathematical question would help your aim?' → optional 1–2 matching suggestions.
Do not always compute Pearson's r. Its purpose is to quantify LINEAR association; a visibly near-perfect line may need different further maths, while curvature may make Pearson a poor summary.
Spearman's rank association is only an optional follow-up for monotonic relationships when it is genuinely suitable and allowed by the student's course/teacher; it doesn't fit every curve.
Do not impose a positive result. Clear lack of an apparent relationship, mixed data, surprises and inconclusive findings can still create valuable reflection and a worthwhile next question.
